title: Aramaic in the Bible
lead: Aramaic, a sister language of Hebrew, became the shared language of the Assyrian, Babylonian and Persian empires. Parts of Ezra and Daniel are written in it, and it was the everyday language of Jesus and his first followers.

sections.b: Two Aramaic words appear in Genesis, when Laban names the heap of witness Jegar-sahadutha (Genesis 31:47). By 701 BC Judah's officials could speak Aramaic, though the people on the wall could not (2 Kings 18:26). After the exile it was the language of empire: Jeremiah 10:11 is an Aramaic sentence, Daniel 2:4–7:28 is in Aramaic, and Ezra quotes Persian letters and tells the story around them in Aramaic (Ezra 4:8–6:18; Ezra 7:12–26). In the time of Jesus most Jews in Galilee and Judea spoke Aramaic; the Gospels keep words such as talitha koum (Mark 5:41), ephphatha (Mark 7:34) and Abba (Mark 14:36), and Jesus' cry from the cross (Mark 15:34). Synagogues read Aramaic translations, the Targums, alongside the Hebrew, and the Talmud is largely in Aramaic. The older name "Chaldee" for biblical Aramaic comes from Daniel 2:4.
